According to a well-regarded leaker with a solid track record, next year could bring the largest iPhone display ever seen.

Supply chain sources indicate Apple is testing a brand-new display that could end up in an iPhone model whose identity remains a mystery…

The Mystery of Next Year's Flagship iPhone Naming

2027 will mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, and it has long been believed Apple is preparing something special to celebrate. That year is expected to be the closest the company has come to realizing the long-held vision of an "all-glass" iPhone.

There have been rumors Apple could release a standalone 20th anniversary edition iPhone, in a fashion similar to the iPhone X. However, more recent reports suggest this revolutionary new design will instead arrive as next year's Pro models, namely the iPhone 19 Pro and Pro Max.

A third possibility is that Apple, in celebration of the anniversary, jumps straight from the iPhone 18 to the iPhone 20.

The Largest iPhone Display Ever

Leaker Digital Chat Station (DCS) reports that supply chain sources indicate Apple is testing the largest iPhone display to date. However, the size increase is only a slight bump up from the 6.9-inch display found on the current iPhone 17 Pro Max.

In other words, they believe Apple will market the device around having a 7-inch display.

DCS has no information on what this new display would be used for—assuming Apple ever puts it into production—but speculates it could be for next year's iPhone Pro Max, though what that model ends up being called remains unknown.

9to5Mac's Take

Apple tests plenty of different things, most of which never see the light of day, so even if this display does exist in prototype form somewhere within the company's supply chain, it doesn't necessarily mean it will end up in an iPhone.

That said, if the company's goal is to achieve an "all-glass" look, being able to tout "the biggest display ever" does seem like it could indeed be a sensible piece of that puzzle.
